question.problem:
Which of the following statements are true?

I. Any $6\times 5$ matrix $A$ has at most $6$ distinct singular values.

II. Any $8\times 9$ matrix $A$ has at most $9$ distinct singular values.

III. The matrix $A=[\begin{aligned}-1 & 0 \\ 0 & -1\end{aligned}]$ has at most two non-negative distinct singular values.
question.worked_solution:
The singular values of the matrix $A$ are the square roots of the eigenvalues of the matrix ${A}^{T}\,A.$ 

With that in mind, let's examine our statements.

- Statement I is false. Since $A$ is a $6\times 5$ matrix and ${A}^{T}$ is a $5\times 6$ matrix, ${A}^{T}\,A$ must be a $5\times 5$ matrix: 

$$
{{A}^{T}}_{5\times 6}\times {A}_{6\times 5}={{A}^{T}\,A}_{5\times 5}
$$

Hence, $A$ has at most $5$ distinct singular values.

- Statement II is true. Indeed, since $A$ is a $8\times 9$ matrix and ${A}^{T}$ is a $9\times 8$ matrix, ${A}^{T}\,A$ must be a $9\times 9$ matrix: 

$$
{{A}^{T}}_{9\times 8}\times {A}_{8\times 9}={{A}^{T}\,A}_{9\times 9}
$$

Hence, $A$ has at most $9$ distinct singular values.

- Statement III is true.  Indeed, all singular values of any matrix are non-negative.

Therefore, the correct answer is "II and III only."
